Is this news? You still have two of the main components of smoking: The nicotine and the habit (smoke after eating, while drinking etc.). The latter one is the main culprit for me personally (I vape 0mg nicotine). Obviously the nicotine and habit part is not much different from the analog cigarettes. But as stated here already, without the thousands of free radicals, carcinogens, tar etc. and the ability to slowly reduce the nicotine amount.

Then I think the ScienceDaily article is misleading. It reads as if this particular research has shown that e-cigs are as addictive to the analog counterparts. The paper does not mention this. It only shows that researchers have successfully employed a known measuring technique (liquid-liquid extraction) to determine concentrations of different types nicotine. And these concentrations seem to vary quite a bit probably because of mislabeling or problems in the manufacturing process. It affects the nicotine uptake as well and therefore the authors suggest studies on how to better standardize and regulate this.

That must've been too boring for ScienceDaily though, so I guess they had to make it a bit more sensational by drawing their own conclusions ... Move along, nothing to see here.

The added ability to vape consistently just makes it easier. I couldn't smoke the way I vape or I would feel terrible. Nonetheless, despite the fact that I vape more than I smoked, I still feel better and healthier, so it works for me.
